newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy welfare talks to start before May 15 - union.
newsitem.headline: Italy welfare talks to start before May 15 - union.

text.p: Talks between the government and unions on reform of the Italian welfare state should start before mid-May, the head of Italy's largest union, the Cgil, said on Wednesday.
"It's in the government's interests to call a meeting on welfare reform before May 15," Sergio Cofferati told reporters.
Union leaders met Prime Minister Romano Prodi for unscheduled talks on Tuesday.
The Cgil has always been adamant that a review of the pensions system, which falls within the overall welfare sector, should not start before 1998.
But the government is under growing pressure to initiate rapidly a reform of social spending to guarantee the sustainability of recent fiscal correction.
"We are waiting to be called to meet the government and we will go with union proposals. We hope that the govenrment comes up with its own proposals," Cofferati said.
The government has said it intends to present an outline of planned welfare spending in its three-year economic programme (DPEF), which is due to be unveiled by the middle of next month.
